messages:
maria-finance: Heads-up — AWS Marketplace sent a credit note that we didn't expect. Invoice INV-2024-0923 shows a credit line of -$12,345 labeled 'Partner Reseller Adjustment'. I'm not sure which partner this maps to or whether it should reduce the customer's next invoice or be applied to our AR aging.
kevin-partner-ops: Thanks for flagging. Do you have the credit note ID and the marketplace order id? Often the partner adjustment is for a channel fee correction. Could be CN-778 or similar.
maria-finance: Attached PDF link in the billing portal: https://redwood.example.com/invoices/INV-2024-0923.pdf — header lists Credit Note CN-778, marketplace order mkt-8921. No partner name in the line item, just "Reseller Adjustment" and tax amount 0.
dana-accounts-payable: If tax is 0, might be AWS-side credit (marketplace-level). We need GL mapping: is this contra-revenue (4000-CR) or an expense write-off (6000-DR)? Also need PO or contract ref to apply to AR. Can someone confirm vendor mapping?
kevin-partner-ops: I pulled mkt-8921 from the partner dashboard. That order was originally associated with Channel Partner ID CP-41 (NorthStar Integrations). I'll confirm with their rep but they reported a pricing rollback last month.
aws-marketplace-bot: Automated notice: Credit Note CN-778 applied to order mkt-8921 on 2024-11-02 10:12 UTC. Affected SKUs: redwood.api.hosted, qty: n/a, amount: -12345.00 USD.
eli-ops: Quick note — this credit looks like it was issued because AWS recalculated the reseller surcharge for Aug usage. It should reduce our net revenue for that month, not be posted as a receivable.
sophie-customer-success: If it's reducing revenue, does that change customer billing? Any affected customers who already got invoices? We had a couple customers charged in Sept for hosted usage.
maria-finance: Good question. The invoice INV-2024-0923 is our payable from AWS, not a customer invoice. So the credit reduces what AWS charges *us*. It shouldn't alter customer invoices already sent. But we need to decide whether to post as negative expense (contra-revenue) vs apply as a prepayment credit to next AWS invoice.
dana-accounts-payable: Requesting approval from Finance Lead to post as contra-revenue in period Oct 2024. If approved, we'll post journal: DR AWS Expense 6000 $12,345, CR Revenue 4000 $12,345 (memo: marketplace reseller adjustment CN-778). @maria-finance can you confirm period?
maria-finance: Period appears to be 2024-08 (usage month). But the note arrived this billing cycle (invoice dated 2024-11-01). Per revenue recognition policy, we should attribute the adjustment to Oct close since that's when the credit was issued. I'll escalate to revenue ops for final ruling.
kevin-partner-ops: I'll ping NorthStar to get their confirmation that CP-41 accepted the adjustment. If they dispute, we may need to hold off posting until resolved.
sophie-customer-success: FYI, NorthStar flagged one customer complaining about a billing mismatch last week — might be related.
eli-ops: For treasury/forecasting: please flag as a one-time revenue adjustment in the November cash forecast. I'll mark it in the model as non-recurring.
maria-finance: Action items: (1) kevin to confirm partner acceptance of CN-778; (2) dana to prepare a draft JE for finance lead review; (3) eli to update forecast; (4) maria to coordinate with revenue ops for period attribution. I'll update thread when I have partner confirmation. :thumbsup:
kevin-partner-ops: On it. Reaching out to NorthStar rep now. Will paste their response here.
aws-marketplace-bot: Reminder: Related documents: https://console.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/credits/CN-778 (requires AWS login).
